articles.title: David Harbour has blown Tony Stark’s cover in Avengers: Doomsday. It might just be what Marvel needs
articles.summary: The actor, who plays Red Guardian in the film, made a cryptic comment to Variety that raised more Robert Downey Jr-shaped questions than answers. But was it a clanger, or expert trolling? Nobody knows exactly what solemn blood oaths Marvel uses to prevent spoilers.
body: Invited by Variety magazine to offer up a line from Doomsday “completely out of context”, Harbour thought for a moment, adopted the Russian accent of his Red Guardian character and came out with: “You … are Tony Stark.” Which is quite a thing to say about a film whose entire marketing campaign so far has depended on us accepting that Iron Man remains dead, and that the actor who used to play him, Robert Downey Jr, is playing Victor von Doom instead.

So what’s going on? The simplest and most likely explanation is that Harbour is trolling us, that Stark is not in the movie at all, and we’re all just fools. The new trailer for Doomsday, premiered last weekend at Disney’s D23 event in Anaheim, leans heavily into the prevailing wisdom that the film’s villain will be the tyrannical, unstoppable baddie of spurious eastern European extraction that Stan Lee and Jack Kirby dreamed up in 1962.

articles.title: ‘We’re barely above porn’: why would a film-maker choose to make a deliberately bad ‘mockbuster’?
articles.summary: With a tiny budget and six days, Anthony Frith directed a film for the studio behind Sharknado – and then made Mockbuster, a documentary about the experience. Directors don’t tend to appreciate having their films eviscerated by critics.
body: This is, however, exactly what I do to the Australian film-maker Anthony Frith. I’ve even prepared a zinger for the occasion. “Your film is a lemon that’s been eaten by a turkey then dumped into a vat of curdled mayonnaise,” I say.
Frith isn’t upset. He even smiles. “That’s a fair assessment,” he replies.

The production I’m sledging isn’t his well-directed, enjoyably staged and sometimes laugh-out-loud funny new documentary Mockbuster. It’s his other film, which Mockbuster charts the making-of: a pulpy, rinky-dink adaptation of The Land That Time Forgot, in which an Australian naval vessel is attacked by a Russian submarine, leaving the crew stranded on a dinosaur-populated island where they’re assaulted by unconvincing accents and various CGI beasts.
points: With a tiny budget and six days, Anthony Frith directed a film for the studio behind Sharknado – and then made Mockbuster, a documentary about the experience.
Directors don’t tend to appreciate having their films eviscerated by critics.

articles.title: TikTok to Pay $400 Million to U.S. Government to Settle Lawsuit Alleging App Violated Child-Safety Law
articles.summary: TikTok, the company behind the popular short-form video app, has agreed to pay $400 million to settle a U.S. government lawsuit alleging that a predecessor app violated the country’s Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA).
body: Since the Justice Department filed the complaint in 2024, “TikTok has undergone significant changes to its ownership, management, compliance functions and privacy practices,” the agency said in announcing the settlement. “The company has implemented extensive measures designed to strengthen safeguards for younger users, improve age-related controls, and enhance parental oversight. Those developments have materially advanced the public interests underlying the Department’s litigation and have strengthened protections for millions of American families.”

In January 2026, under a deal brokered by the Trump administration, ByteDance sold a majority stake in TikTok’s U.S. business to non-Chinese investors, including Oracle, Silver Lake and Abu Dhabi’s state-owned investment firm MGX. Beijing-based ByteDance retains 19.9% of the joint venture; the deal brought ByteDance and TikTok into compliance with the U.S.’s TikTok divest-or-ban law that went into effect in January 2025.

articles.title: LISTEN: Amazon Courts Creators to Build Businesses and Scale the Attention Economy for Brands
articles.summary: On today’s episode of Variety‘s “Strictly Business” podcast, Matt Sandler and Angie More of Amazon explain how the digital behemoth is diving in to the creator economy to build business and bring scale in ad buying to big brands.
body: The pair point to the burgeoning cottage industry around the Jason and Travis Kelce podcast “New Heights.” That show is the hub of a wheel that includes the Amazon-built e-commerce storefront Kelce Clubhouse, which sells a range of fan and lifestyle merch, not all of which is directly related to the sibling NFL players. The multifaceted Keke Palmer has also teamed with Amazon Creator Services for her “Baby, this is Keke Palmer” podcast that has led to other pacts in the Amazon-verse including Palmer’s plan to go live on Twitch twice a month.

The array of options that creators pursue is part of the sizzle of the sector and something that greatly appeals to brands. Sandler and More’s work is to make it more adaptable and, yes, scalable for marketers.

articles.title: Shaquille O’Neal: Marvel Turned Me Down for the ‘Avengers’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Shaquille O’Neal will not be appearing in December’s “Avengers: Doomsday,” or any other “Avengers” film, for that matter. In an interview with Variety about his “Dunkman” league, the first professional dunking league where contestants from around the world compete for a grand prize of $500,000 …
body: The NBA legend desperately wanted to join the MCU but the powers that be were not as enthused by the idea. He also really wants to fight The Rock.

While O’Neal, 54, portrayed a DC superhero in 1997’s “Steel,” he says he’s spent years trying to be a part of the Marvel Cinematic Universe — namely, in an “Avengers” movie — but was rebuffed by the studio. He’d first made his desire to be in an “Avengers” movie known during a 2018 interview with EW.

“I wanted to be in the ‘Avengers’ and they were like, ‘Shaq, we fuckin’ love you and we’d love to put you in, but if your face pops up on screen people are going to go, ‘Hey, that’s Shaq!’ He said it truthfully, and I was like, alright… I guess my face is too bigtime.”

O’Neal did pop up in a fun cameo at the end of this year’s “Scary Movie,” and will also appear in “Grown Ups 3.” But now that the Marvel dream has died, he’s keen on sharing the silver screen with another hulking star, Dwayne “ The Rock ” Johnson.

articles.title: Prince Harry and six others face privacy case legal bill of up to £34.5m
articles.summary: The seven claimants, who include Sir Elton John and Liz Hurley, have to pay the Daily Mail publisher an initial £9.54m in the next seven days after losing a privacy case.
body: Prince Harry and six other public figures face paying up to £34.5m to the publisher of the Daily Mail after a High Court judge imposed an exceptional order for legal costs over their failed privacy case.
The seven claimants, also including Sir Elton John and Liz Hurley, must pay an initial £9.54m by Friday of next week to Associated Newspapers Limited (ANL).

The judge ruled that the case was a rare one in which the claimants should have to pay far in excess of the costs that had been agreed before trial, criticising how they presented their claims as "unreasonable to a high degree".
On 7 July, Judge Mr Justice Nicklin dismissed the claims of unlawful information-gathering, which ANL denied.

articles.title: The Odyssey becomes highest grossing R-rated film of all time
articles.summary: Christopher Nolan’s epic has achieved $1.35bn at the global box office, overtaking 2024’s Deadpool & Wolverine. The Odyssey has overtaken Deadpool & Wolverine to become the highest grossing R-rated film of all time.
body: According to figures compiled by the Numbers, Christopher Nolan’s adaptation of Homer’s epic poem has achieved $1.35bn (£990m) at the worldwide box office, compared with the Ryan Reynolds/Hugh Jackman superhero movie, which stands at $1.34bn (£980m) since its release in 2024.

A R-rating as designated by the Motion Picture Association requires anyone under 17 to be accompanied by an adult, and is normally seen as a brake on box office expectations. In its citation, the MPA said The Odyssey was given an R-rating “for violence and some language”.
In the UK, The Odyssey has been rated 15 for “strong violence”, while in Australia it has an M-rating for “mature themes, violence and coarse language”.

Other R-rated features to do well include Nolan’s previous film Oppenheimer, which benefited from the “Barbenheimer” craze to amass $983m worldwide, the Joaquin Phoenix-starring Joker ($1.1bn), and the two standalone Deadpool movies ($782m and $786m respectively).

articles.title: Meghan in talks for role in Netflix series The Gentlemen, BBC understands
articles.summary: This would be Meghan's first significant acting role since her marriage to Prince Harry.
body: The Duchess of Sussex is in talks to return to acting with a role in Netflix series The Gentlemen, the BBC has learned.

Much of the two previous series of The Gentlemen, which was created by Guy Ritchie, have been filmed in the Cotswolds - the area it is rumoured Harry and Meghan will set up home when they return to the UK later this month.
The Gentlemen, starring the actor Theo James, is a comedy series about a duke who becomes a drug baron.
The details of the discussions and any role Meghan might be offered have not yet been revealed.

articles.title: Tupac murder accused told police in 2008 his nephew fired fatal shots
articles.summary: A recording of the interview Duane Davis conducted with detectives was played to the jury.
body: The man accused of orchestrating the murder of Tupac Shakur told police more than a decade later that he handed the gun used in the drive-by shooting to a passenger who then passed it to his nephew who opened fire on the rapper.

Duane "Keffe D" Davis is on trial in Las Vegas, charged with one count of murder with a deadly weapon over the killing of the rap superstar in 1996. On Thursday jurors heard a recording of a police interview with Davis in 2008.
Prosecutors allege that although Davis did not fire the gun that killed Shakur, he ordered the shooting and supplied the deadly weapon to further criminal conduct for the gang he helped lead.
His lawyer Michael Sanft has argued that what his client had previously said of his involvement cannot be believed.

articles.title: ‘Task’ Star Tom Pelphrey on Finding Himself in His Devoted Dad Role — and Nearly Playing Professor X
articles.summary: The two-time Emmy nominee was a runner-up for the new 'X-Men' movie, and jokes that at least audiences won't have to see him bald: "The only hat I can wear is a fitted size eight. It is empirically a big fat head, and I don't know if we want to see it shaved."
body: In 2020, Tom Pelphrey made waves on Ozark season three, paving the way for his first Primetime Emmy nomination the following season. The development came as no surprise to fans of his mid-2010s pulpy action series, Banshee. The New Jersey native had likewise joined that low-key critical darling during its third season, and his magnetic turn as Kurt Bunker quickly became a fan favorite — earning him a promotion to series regular ahead of the fourth-and-final season.

His sheriff’s deputy character didn’t necessarily struggle with substance abuse; he was a reformed white supremacist desperately trying to atone for his past. But he couldn’t afford to remove the visible tattoos that marked his former affiliation, and Pelphrey intricately captured the inner conflict of confronting one’s greatest regret every time Bunker looked in the mirror.
points: The two-time Emmy nominee was a runner-up for the new 'X-Men' movie, and jokes that at least audiences won't have to see him bald: "The only hat I can wear is a fitted size eight.
It is empirically a big fat head, and I don't know if we want to see it shaved."
